title: Alibi and Confession
premise: Estate lawyer Lena Almeida is hired by a dying man, Tomas Reyes, to prove that a murder he confessed to thirty years ago never actually happened — because the victim, his business partner, has apparently been alive all along and is now claiming the estate. As Lena digs into forged death certificates, swapped identities, and an alibi built on a night no one will discuss, she discovers Tomas paid her not to clear his name but to find the man before the man finds him. The climax forces Lena to choose between exposing a decades-old fraud that would destroy the found family Tomas built, or letting a guilty man die believing himself forgiven. She chooses truth with mercy: the 'victim' is exposed as the real killer who faked his own death, Tomas dies at peace, and Lena inherits not the case but the family she never meant to keep.
about_author: Mirabel Okonkwo is a former probate clerk in Lagos and Lisbon who spent a decade reading other people's final wishes before writing her own stories. She writes mysteries about paperwork, secrets, and the families we assemble from strangers.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A retainer arrives with payment in full and one impossible instruction: prove a 1994 murder never happened. The client, Tomas Reyes, is dying and refuses to meet in person. Lena, who prides herself on closable cases, almost declines — until she finds the victim's name on a living person's tax records. Beat: cold curiosity igniting into obsession.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the coastal town of Vila Serena, Lena interviews the executor, Marta, who managed Tomas's affairs for decades and treats Lena's questions as betrayal. The official record says partner Duarte Fonseca drowned; the harbor remembers otherwise. A threatening note appears in Lena's rental car. Beat: first taste of danger, and the sense everyone is protecting someone.

chapters.title: An Alibi in Amber
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV, via recorded tapes he mailed years ago. He recounts the night of the drowning: an argument over money, a storm, a body he swears he pulled from the water alive — then lost in the dark. His voice cracks when describing Duarte's daughter, Sofia, whom he raised afterward. Beat: sympathy for a self-confessed killer; the alibi begins to feel like penance.

chapters.title: The Living Dead Man
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following financial threads, Lena finds 'Duarte Fonseca' alive under another name in Porto — but the man she confronts denies being Duarte, then offers her money to stop. Someone else is watching them both. Sofia arrives unannounced, demanding to know why a lawyer is digging up her father's grave. Beat: the mystery doubles; trust becomes currency.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sofia's POV. Sofia reveals she always suspected her father didn't drown — he sent money anonymously for years after his 'death.' She and Lena form an uneasy alliance, trading childhood memories for legal documents. They discover the death certificate was signed by a doctor who died mysteriously a year later. Beat: found family forming between two women raised by lies.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Kept
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. An old fisherman finally talks: there were two men in the boat that night, and only one came back to shore — but not the one the town thinks. Meanwhile Marta burns a box of letters and confesses she's been paying blackmail for twenty years. Beat: the protective silence around Tomas revealed as fear, not loyalty.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Dying, Tomas summons Lena at last and tells the whole truth: he helped fake Duarte's death to save him from creditors — until Duarte turned extortionist and threatened Sofia. Tomas confessed to a murder that never happened to give Duarte a clean escape. Now Duarte wants the estate, and Tomas wants absolution. Beat: love against duty crystallized; Lena realizes she was hired as a shield.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Duarte escalates: he files a claim on the estate and implicates Lena in evidence tampering. Racing the clock, Lena uncovers proof the Porto man isn't Duarte at all — he's the doctor's son, wearing his father's fraud like an inheritance. The real Duarte has been closer than anyone guessed. Beat: rising dread; every ally is compromised.

chapters.title: Vila Serena, After Dark
chapters.summary: Lena and Sofia's POV, alternating. The real Duarte — Marta's brother, hidden in plain sight — comes for the estate papers and for Tomas. Confrontation at the cliffside house: confessions, a near-drowning mirroring 1994, and Lena choosing to hand over the evidence that convicts rather than the lie that protects. Beat: climax; duty wins, but at visible cost.

chapters.title: Everything Left Unspoken
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, epilogue months later. Tomas dies holding Sofia's hand, forgiven by the daughter of the man he didn't kill. The estate passes to Sofia and Marta; Lena closes the file but keeps the family, staying in Vila Serena through the winter. Final line echoes the retainer letter: some cases close you instead. Beat: bittersweet resolution; survival's price paid, love's dividend collected.
